study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative trajectories of R1, R2*, and magnetic susceptibility in basal ganglia on healthy ageing

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To establish normative trajectories of R1, R2*, and magnetic susceptibility in the basal ganglia at 3T using a healthy ageing cohort with evenly distributed age (18-80 years) and sex ratio throughout adulthood, and to validate these trajectories using an independent cohort comprising both healthy participants and individuals with Parkinson's disease.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper provides detailed description of preprocessing steps including skull stripping tool (SynthStrip), susceptibility mapping pipeline (SEPIA with specific steps), R2* processing (MP-PCA denoising), R1 processing (dictionary matching with B1 correction), and registration procedures (ANTs for nonlinear registration to MNI space using MuSus-100 atlas).
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: SynthStrip (Hoopes et al., 2022) was used for skull stripping on the second inversion time of the R1 data (INV2, proton density contrast) with the ABRIM cohort or the MPRAGE image with the PPP cohort, and the first echo of the GRE data (GRE1). For χ processing, the GRE brain masks were first refined by excluding voxels with high R2* values on the brain mask edge to improve estimation robustness. χ maps were derived using SEPIA v1.2.2.4 (Chan & Marques, 2021) with the following pipeline: bipolar gradient phase correction (J. Li et al., 2015), ROMEO (Dymerska et al., 2021) for total field computation, V-SHARP (W. Li et al., 2011) for background field removal, and LP-CNN (Lai et al., 2020) for dipole field inversion... For R2* mapping, Marchenko-Pastur Principal Component Analysis (MP-PCA) denoising (Veraart et al., 2016) with a patch size of 5 x 5 x 5 voxels was applied to the complex-valued mGRE data to improve SNR and the magnitude of the denoised data was then extracted to derive R2* maps based on a closed-form solution (Gil et al., 2016). Quantitative R1 maps were obtained using the BIDS-compatible Matlab function 'bids_T1B1correct.m' hosted on GitHub... All data and statistical analyses were conducted in the common MNI space (ICBM 2009c Nonlinear Asymmetric) (Fonov et al., 2009). The MuSus-100 atlas (He et al., 2022) was used to provide parcellation labels of the basal ganglia, including detailed thalamic sub-regions.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests were used to compare z-scores and median qMRI values between healthy controls and Parkinson's disease patients for each subcortical structure. The Benjamini and Hochberg procedure was used to control the false discovery rate (FDR) at 0.05. An adjusted p-value of 0.05 after FDR correction was considered statistically significant. Separate comparisons were made between: (1) PPP PD patients vs PPP healthy controls, and (2) PPP PD patients vs ABRIM healthy controls. Statistical significance levels were reported as * p < 0.05; ** p < 0.01; *** p < 0.001.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative trajectories showed R1 predominantly exhibits quadratic shape over age in basal ganglia, while R2* and magnetic susceptibility are primarily linear; substantia nigra (both SNc and SNr) showed significantly higher R2* and χ in Parkinson's disease patients compared to healthy controls (adjusted p < 0.001), validating the clinical utility of these normative models.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study established normative trajectories for R1, R2*, and χ in 11 subcortical structures and multiple thalamic sub-nuclei using GPR in 260 healthy adults (18-79 years). R1 trajectories showed inverted U-shape with peaks between 45-60 years, while R2* and χ were predominantly linear. Spatial gradients in putamen and caudate nucleus also changed with age, particularly in lateral-medial direction for R2* and χ. Validation on the independent PPP cohort (44 healthy controls, 316 PD patients) showed that: (1) healthy controls' z-scores fell within |z| ≤ 1.96 for most structures, (2) PD patients showed significantly elevated R2* and χ in substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc: adjusted p = 6.8×10^-7 and 1.5×10^-3 for R2* and χ) and substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr: adjusted p = 5.8×10^-3 and 0.018), (3) when comparing PD patients to ABRIM controls, additional structures (NAcc, RN, VP, thalamus) also showed highly significant differences (p < 0.001). Strong correlations were observed between R2* and χ z-scores (R = 0.44-0.81) across structures, while correlations with R1 were weaker (R = 0.17-0.39), indicating partially independent information. The normative models derived from wider age range (ABRIM) were smoother and more robust than those from narrower age range (PPP controls).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study demonstrated that normative models can successfully be applied across datasets with similar but not identical acquisition protocols (MP2RAGE vs MPRAGE for structural imaging). Increasing the control population size (comparing PPP controls vs ABRIM controls) resulted in more regions showing highly significant differences with PD patients, highlighting the value of large normative datasets. The study also explored correlation networks of deviations, identifying two main 'networks of variations' in iron-sensitive measures: one comprising caudate nucleus and putamen, and another including globus pallidus, substantia nigra, red nucleus, ventral pallidum, and subthalamic nucleus. Higher-order statistics (IQR, skewness) and spatial gradients showed potential as additional biomarkers but were noisier than median values.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study focused exclusively on 3T data, with detailed qMRI protocols including MP2RAGE for R1 mapping (dictionary matching approach rather than lookup table), multi-echo GRE for R2*/susceptibility mapping with 9 echoes at 0.8mm isotropic resolution. The study included both subcortical structures (11 ROIs) and detailed thalamic sub-nuclei from MuSus-100 atlas. An alternative atlas (AHEAD) was also evaluated in supplementary materials to demonstrate robustness. The ABRIM dataset and processing scripts are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.34973/atyn-r066. For the PPP dataset, a separate data access agreement is required. The study implemented a sophisticated 4-step hybrid image registration procedure combining R1 and χ maps for improved subcortical parcellation accuracy. Retrospective correction was applied for datasets with tilted field-of-view relative to B0 direction. The study compared dictionary matching vs lookup table approaches for MP2RAGE T1 mapping in supplementary materials, showing dictionary matching provides better T1 estimates in CSF regions and partial volume areas. For Parkinson's disease patients, all were within 5 years of diagnosis, and only baseline scans were used.
